chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: The Plantation in Culver City and Mike Lyman
summary: Mike Lyman wired Spikes in New York to put a band into the Plantation, so Ory's band played there; Lyman and his brother had changed their name from Simon.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. And when I was...went to New York with that picture you saw me up on the bootblack stand, they opened the Plantation in Culver City--the Plantation night club--and Lyman wired me in New York to come and put the band in there. So when I came back to put the band in there, we put Mutt and them in there--Kid Ory and them in there. I didn't have no band. In the music store, every time I got a job, I'd get three or
four guys, and we'd go fill it, you know.
Was that Mike Lyman or Abe Lyman?
Mike Lyman--because he had the restaurant business, right?
Yeah. Well, he...at that time, Mike...when I...I told you when I was playing for Rudolph Valentino, Mike Lyman was a singer. Mike.
And then he later opened what--a restaurant downtown, right?
Yeah, on Eighth and Hill, I think. Or Seventh and Eighth and Hill or somewhere. Mike Lyman's place.
And then later--much later on--he had a place in Hollywood, too. He had two--one downtown and one in Hollywood.

I don't know. You know, their name wasn't Lyman. Their name was Simon, so he had a couple of brothers called Simon, and he and Abe changed their name to Lyman...during the war or something like that, they didn't want to be Jewish or something. And they...now he had a couple of brothers named Simon.
Yeah, but they were in partners together but one was called Simon, one was called Lyman.
